brief.premise: a forest toll road where the levy is counted in felled timber
brief.storyline: the player is looking for a sibling who took the warden's badge and stopped writing
brief.tone: damp, wry, and short of daylight
brief.protagonist: a timber-tallier walking the road out of season

title: The Hollow Tithe
blurb: A toll road, a levy counted in timber, and a warden who stopped writing home.

lore.title: The Hollow Tithe
lore.premise: The crown stopped asking for coin three winters ago and started asking for timber. The forest has been paying ever since, and the road that carries it is the only law out here.
lore.era: the third winter of the timber levy
lore.tone: damp, wry, and short of daylight

regions.name: The Long Fell
regions.blurb: Deep forest cut by one road and a hundred arguments about who owns the trees beside it.
regions.culture: Fellers and cart-drivers who count in cords and trust in writing.
lore: A cord of oak buys more here than a purse of silver.
The Compact keeps its own tally, and it does not match the crown's.
ambient: The canopy closes over the road and the light goes green.
Somewhere off the track, an axe stops mid-stroke.
Sap has stuck your sleeve to your arm again.

regions.name: The Warden's Shoulder
regions.blurb: High open ground where the road climbs out of the trees and the crown can finally see it.
regions.culture: Wardens, weighers and people who have learned to be elsewhere.
lore: Every cart is weighed twice on the Shoulder, and the second weight is the one that counts.
ambient: The wind up here has nothing to break it.
You can see the road for a mile in both directions, which is the point.

sites.name: Bracken Cross
sites.description: Three roads meet under trees old enough to have opinions. Everything here smells of wet sawdust and everyone here is waiting for a cart.

npcs.name: Ilse Marrow
npcs.appearance: Broad, wind-burnt, two fingers short on her left hand and unbothered about it.
npcs.persona: Blunt, fair, and counting something the whole time she talks to you.
knows: A warden came through in autumn with a new badge and would not give a name.
The Cord House tally has been short every month since the levy doubled.
Nobody has walked the high road past the fort since the first frost.

npcs.name: Bevan Halloway
npcs.appearance: Grey, deliberate, hands scarred pale across the knuckles.
npcs.persona: Answers the question you asked and not the one you meant.
knows: He re-shod a warden's horse in autumn and was paid in crown paper, which nobody here will take.
His daughter took the road east and has not written either.

npcs.name: Sedge
npcs.appearance: Thin, cheerful, wearing three coats none of which fit.
npcs.persona: Talks to fill the silence and does not much mind what with.
knows: The weighbridge on the Shoulder gives a different number going up than coming down.
A cord of oak is worth a week's wage and worth losing a hand over.

hooks: The Cord House tally has come up short every month since the levy doubled.

sites.name: Stonewait
sites.description: A weighing station that grew walls. The road runs straight through it and stops, twice, whether you like it or not.

npcs.name: Warden Cull
npcs.appearance: Neat, tired, badge polished past the point of vanity.
npcs.persona: Correct about everything and comfortable about none of it.
knows: The badge you are asking after was signed out in autumn and never signed back in.
Two tallies leave this station: one for the crown and one that is true.

npcs.name: Ott Pell
npcs.persona: Would rather show you the ledger than argue with you about it.
knows: The autumn warden walked east off the road and left the horse behind.
He keeps his own copy of every weight, and he keeps it somewhere else.

hooks: A warden's badge was signed out in autumn and never signed back in.

sites.name: Harrowmere
sites.description: Where the timber finally stops being timber and starts being money. The biggest place on the road and the one least interested in the forest that pays for it.

npcs.name: Factor Odell
npcs.appearance: Comfortable, courteous, sleeves too clean for the trade he is in.
npcs.persona: Agrees with you warmly and concedes nothing.
knows: He buys crown paper at four parts in five and does not ask where it came from.
A warden sold him a full ledger in autumn and asked to be forgotten.

npcs.name: Meret Sallow
npcs.appearance: Young, precise, one sleeve permanently pushed up.
npcs.persona: Frightened of the ledger and unable to leave it alone.
knows: The Crown Yard receives more cord than the road can carry.
Somebody has been signing the difference off in a hand she recognises.

hooks: The Crown Yard takes in more timber than the road could possibly deliver.

arc.title: The Hollow Tithe
arc.premise: Your sister took the warden's badge, walked the road east, and stopped writing. The tally she was keeping stopped adding up at about the same time.

beats.journal: Ilse Marrow says a warden came through in autumn with a new badge and no name, and that the Cord House tally has been short ever since.

quest.name: Read the Cord House tally
quest.description: Ilse keeps her own count. Get a copy of it and take it up the road.

beats.journal: Warden Cull confirms it: the badge was signed out in autumn and never signed back in. Two tallies leave Stonewait, and only one of them is true.

quest.name: Find who kept the true weight
quest.description: Ott Pell keeps his own copy of every weight. Ask him where it goes.

beats.journal: Factor Odell bought a full ledger from a warden in autumn, at four parts in five, and was asked to forget her. He remembers the hand it was written in. So do you.

card.title: The hand you know
card.subtitle: read in the back room of Odell's, by one lamp

sections.heading: The ledger
sections.body: It is not the crown's book and it was never meant to be. Two columns to a page: what the road carried, and what the yard received. The second is always the larger, and the difference is always about a cord, and it has been about a cord every month since the levy doubled.

sections.heading: The hand
sections.body: Small, hard, and slanted to the left, the way she wrote everything from the time she was nine. She kept the true count for three winters, sold it to a man who buys paper and does not ask, and asked him to forget her. She did not stop writing. She stopped writing to you.

nodes.speech: Out of season and on foot. You are either lost or you are looking for somebody.

choices.text: Looking for a warden. New badge, autumn.
What is wrong with the tally here?

nodes.speech: She came through, yes. Would not give a name, which around here is the same as giving one. Went up toward Stonewait and did not come back down.

choices.text: That is enough to go on.

nodes.speech: Short. Every month since the levy doubled, and always by about a cord. I keep my own count because I am not a fool. Here — take a copy up the road and see whose face changes.

actions.description: Ilse's own count, in a small hard hand, folded twice.

nodes.speech: You still have my count, I see. Good. It is worth more out of this house than in it.
Back again. There is stew, and there is the other stew.
The road is open and the weighbridge is not. State your business or use the verge.

choices.text: I am looking for a warden.

nodes.speech: You are carrying paper. I can always tell. Whose is it?
Signed out in autumn. Never signed back in. I have written it up four times and four times it has come back initialled and unread.
Two tallies leave this station. One goes to the crown and one is true. I sign both, which is the part I would rather you did not write down.
Ott keeps the honest weight and Ott does not keep it here. Ask him, not me. He is on the bench because I cannot bear to watch him do sums.
Still here. Still open. Still not the weighbridge.
Paper, timber, or trouble? I buy the first, weigh the second, and price the third rather high.

choices.text: A ledger, sold to you in autumn.
Why does the Crown Yard take more cord than the road carries?

nodes.speech: A warden, yes. Four parts in five, which was generous, and she asked to be forgotten, which was cheap. I have an excellent memory and a very short one, depending.
Because the road is not the only way in, and the yard is not the only one counting. You did not need me to tell you that. You needed somebody to say it out loud.
On whether the person asking is family. You have her hand about the mouth, if not the sense. It is in the back, and it is not for sale twice.

choices.text: Then I will read it here.

nodes.speech: Back. The ledger has not moved and neither have I.
